_meta.source: Official seasonal forecasts and outlooks, hand-curated; each opened and its quote checked by a second reader
notes: Forecasts, not events: what national weather services, regional climate outlook forums, FEWS NET and SADC expect for a place in the months listed, as issued between August and September 2026.
Attributed means the forecaster names El Niño as a driver; consistent means it does not, but the expected rain fits El Niño’s usual pattern there.
A selection of food-relevant forecasts, not a complete list. Not yet covered: India (the north-east monsoon forecast was not out), Bangladesh, Argentina, Mexico, Thailand and Vietnam.

events.title: Afghanistan: wet start to the wet season
events.likelihood: expected above-average precipitation
events.place: Afghanistan (countrywide; point in the northern wheat belt)
events.why: FEWS NET expects above-average and timely winter wheat planting after four drought years from 2021 to 2024, and better snowpack if temperatures stay average to below average.
events.quote: The ongoing El Niño event is expected to drive above-average precipitation countrywide between October 2026 and January 2027

source.title: Afghanistan Food Security Outlook Update August 2026 - January 2027: Crisis (IPC Phase 3) persists despite an anticipated favorable start to the season

events.title: Southern Africa: dry start to the season
events.likelihood: increased chances of below-normal rainfall (high confidence)
events.place: Angola, southern Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Namibia, Botswana, most of South Africa, Eswatini, Lesotho (point in Gaza province, Mozambique)
events.why: SADC's regional consensus for the planting months. It expects El Nino to peak around October to December at strong to very strong intensity. Most of the DRC, northern Zambia, central Malawi and northern Mozambique are the exception, with normal to above-normal rain favoured.
events.quote: Much of Angola, southern Zambia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Namibia, Botswana, most of South Africa, Eswatini and Lesotho. Increased chances of below-normal rainfall (High confidence).

source.title: Statement from the Thirty-Third Southern Africa Regional Climate Outlook Forum (SARCOF-33)

events.title: Drought to deepen on the NSW Northern Tablelands
events.likelihood: most likely outcome at 30 November (mode of the 99-member ensemble)
events.place: Northern Tablelands, west of Glen Innes, New South Wales
events.why: NSW DPIRD's drought forecast to 30 Nov, built on BoM's 99-member ACCESS-S ensemble, has drought persisting across central, northern and eastern NSW, with about 35% of the state in a drought category (range 22 to 45%). BoM's newer 24 Sep outlook favours above-average Oct to Dec rain in north-east NSW, which could ease this.
events.quote: Areas of the Northern Tablelands are likely to transition into the NSW-CDI Intense Drought category (e.g., west of Glen Innes).

source.title: Drought forecast (State Seasonal Update, August 2026)
source.publisher: NSW Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development

events.title: Dry Oct to Dec for southern and eastern Victoria and Tasmania
events.likelihood: likely (60 to 80% chance) below average
events.place: Southern and eastern Victoria and Tasmania, Australia
events.why: The Bureau of Meteorology's ACCESS-S outlook issued 24 Sep puts below-average Oct to Dec rain as likely here. It also gives over 80% chance of unusually high daytime temperatures across most of Victoria and Tasmania.
events.quote: Below average rainfall is likely (60 to 80% chance) for much of southern and eastern Victoria, Tasmania

source.title: Climate outlook for October to January

events.title: Dry October across much of the NT, Queensland and the south-east
events.likelihood: likely (60% to greater than 80% chance) below average
events.place: Much of the Northern Territory, Queensland and south-east Australia (point in central-west Queensland)
events.why: In the same 24 Sep outlook, the October-only dry signal covers a much wider area than the three-month signal. For Oct to Dec as a whole, BoM favours above-average rain in western and southern Queensland, so the dry signal here is for October.
events.quote: For October alone, there is a broader dry signal with rainfall likely (60% to greater than 80% chance) to be below average

source.title: Climate outlook for October to January

events.title: Higher spring fire risk in northern and south-eastern NSW
events.likelihood: heightened risk of fire for spring
events.place: South-eastern New South Wales (also northern NSW and south-east Queensland)
events.why: AFAC prepared its spring outlook with BoM and the state fire agencies. It says the NSW and Queensland risk is driven by low soil moisture, and that these NSW areas are warmer and drier than normal.
events.quote: fire authorities predicting a heightened risk of fire across northern and southeastern New South Wales, south-east Queensland, northeastern Tasmania

source.title: Seasonal Bushfire Outlook Spring 2026
source.publisher: AFAC (Australasian Fire and Emergency Service Authorities Council)

events.title: Late wet-season onset in the Top End and north and east Queensland
events.likelihood: 55 to 80% chance of a later than normal onset
events.place: Top End of the Northern Territory and northern and eastern Queensland
events.why: In its final 2026-27 issue, BoM expects the first 50 mm of rain after 1 September, roughly what plants need to start growing, to arrive later than normal here. The page says onset tends to come later in El Nino years. The 24 Sep outlook also has below-average Oct to Dec rain likely for the northern Top End and Cape York.
events.quote: Northern and eastern Queensland and the Top End of the Northern Territory have a 55–80% chance of a later than normal northern rainfall onset.

source.title: Northern rainfall onset outlook

events.title: Wet Oct to Dec across most of Western Australia
events.likelihood: likely (60% to greater than 80% chance) above average; 50 to 80% chance of unusually high rainfall in southern and central WA
events.place: Southern and central Western Australia
events.why: The 24 Sep outlook favours above-average rain over most of WA, with a 50 to 80% chance of totals in the wettest 20% of records in southern and central parts. BoM notes that seas west of Australia are forecast to warm, which can fuel rain systems.
events.quote: October to December rainfall is likely (60% to greater than 80% chance) to be above average across most of Western Australia

source.title: Climate outlook for October to January

events.title: Wetter Oct to Dec favoured for southern Queensland and north-east NSW
events.likelihood: likely (60% to greater than 80% chance) above average for Oct to Dec as a whole
events.place: Western and southern Queensland and north-east New South Wales (point on the Darling Downs)
events.why: The same 24 Sep outlook extends the western wet signal into western and southern Queensland and north-east NSW. October alone leans dry here, so the wet signal is for the three months together. It is newer than the NSW drought forecast of 31 Aug and could ease it.
events.quote: the southern two-thirds of the Northern Territory, western and southern Queensland, and north-east New South Wales

source.title: Climate outlook for October to January

events.title: Below average rain for soy sowing in MATOPIBA and Mato Grosso
events.likelihood: below average for October to December
events.place: MATOPIBA (Maranhao, Tocantins, Piaui, Bahia) and Mato Grosso, Brazil
events.why: Spring is when the main summer crops are sown. The joint INMET, INPE and Funceme outlook places below-average rain over Mato Grosso and MATOPIBA and above-average temperatures over most of Brazil. INMET says El Nino is generally linked to less rain in the north and northeast and that this forecast fits that pattern.
events.quote: precipitação abaixo da média em grande da Região Norte, em Mato Grosso e na região agrícola do MATOPIBA, entre Maranhão, Tocantins, Piauí e Bahia

source.title: Primavera comeca com chuvas acima da media no Centro-Sul e abaixo da media em partes do Norte e Nordeste

events.title: Wetter than average spring in southern Brazil
events.likelihood: above average; totals may exceed the October to December average by up to 200 mm
events.place: Southern Brazil (Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, Parana)
events.why: The outlook expects above-average rain across the South Region, strongest in Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina and southern and eastern Parana, where totals may exceed the season average by up to 200 mm. INMET links more rain in the south to El Nino.
events.quote: O mapa mostra o predomínio de anomalias positivas de precipitação na Região Sul, principalmente no Rio Grande do Sul, em Santa Catarina

source.title: Primavera comeca com chuvas acima da media no Centro-Sul e abaixo da media em partes do Norte e Nordeste

events.title: Wet autumn south of the Yangtze
events.likelihood: markedly above normal (明显偏多), with a high chance of extreme rain events
events.place: Jiangnan and eastern south-west China
events.why: At its September press conference, the China Meteorological Administration said that under El Nino, autumn rain across the Yangtze basin and southwards would mostly be above normal, markedly so in Jiangnan and eastern south-west China, with a high chance of extreme rain events.
events.quote: 受厄尔尼诺影响，秋季我国长江流域及以南大部分地区降水以偏多为主，其中江南和西南地区东部降水明显偏多

source.title: 中国气象局2026年9月新闻发布会 (CMA September 2026 press conference)

events.title: Drier than normal months ahead in Colombia's Andean region
events.likelihood: about 70% chance below normal in December; 50 to 70% in October
events.place: Andean region of Colombia
events.why: IDEAM expects below-normal rain as El Nino strengthens, with December cuts of 60 to 80 percent (about 50 to 150 mm) and January cuts of 50 to 80 percent in the Andean region. November is mostly below normal with local exceptions. February and March may turn wetter, with lower confidence.
events.quote: Región Andina: el modelo probabilístico favorece precipitación por debajo de lo normal en la totalidad de la región con probabilidades cercanas a 70 %.

source.title: Informe de prediccion climatica a corto, mediano y largo plazo (octubre 2026 a marzo 2027)

events.title: Northern Ethiopia and Sudan: dry spell runs into October
events.likelihood: likely (below-average rainfall persisting through October)
events.place: Central and northern Ethiopia, Sudan pastoral belt, Eritrea, Djibouti
events.why: These areas got less than 60% of normal rain from 1 June to 25 August, among the driest seasons on record in the worst-hit places. ICPAC keeps rain below average through October, the end of the season. Field reports from northern Ethiopia show delayed planting, poor germination and crop wilting. The report ties the dry west of the region to El Nino.
events.quote: ICPAC forecasts indicate that below-average rainfall and above-average temperatures are likely to persist in these affected areas between August and October.

source.title: Special Report: Strengthening El Nino Conditions: Implications for Rainfall, Flood Risk and Food Security in Eastern Africa
source.publisher: Food Security and Nutrition Working Group (FSNWG), published by ICPAC

events.title: Below normal rain for Fiji's sugarcane belt
events.likelihood: below normal; October rain likely suppressed, November still favours dry conditions
events.place: Western Viti Levu sugarcane belt (Olosara-Tavua corridor), Fiji
events.why: The Fiji Meteorological Service and the Sugar Research Institute of Fiji advise against new planting in the driest sectors until rain comes and warn that dry trash raises the risk of cane fires. They say El Nino events in Fiji are commonly linked to reduced rain and dry spells.
events.quote: With El Niño expected to continue and rainfall remaining below normal, conserving soil moisture is essential.

source.title: Fiji Sugarcane Rainfall Outlook, September 2026
source.publisher: Fiji Meteorological Service and Sugar Research Institute of Fiji

events.title: Early end to the rainy season in Honduras and Nicaragua
events.likelihood: early end of the rains expected (qualitative)
events.place: Central American Dry Corridor, Honduras and Nicaragua (point near Choluteca)
events.why: FEWS NET reports rain deficits and heat since late June that put the Segunda basic grain season at risk in most of Central America. It says late September rain comes too late to help crops, and expects the rainy season to end early in Honduras, Nicaragua and parts of Venezuela.
events.quote: sin embargo, se espera una finalización temprana de la temporada de lluvias

source.title: Monitoreo Estacional America Latina y el Caribe, septiembre 23, 2026: Deficit de humedad en Pacifico de Centroamerica

events.title: Rainfall deficits likely in Hispaniola and Puerto Rico
events.likelihood: unusually low rainfall likely (high confidence)
events.place: Hispaniola and Puerto Rico
events.why: CariCOF expects fewer showers, wet spells and heavy rain events than usual in the late wet season because of the very strong El Nino. Most islands already carry rainfall deficits after an unusually dry first half of the wet season.
events.quote: with the highest chances for rainfall deficits in coming months in Hispaniola, Puerto Rico, the US Virgin Islands, the Lesser Antilles, and the ABC Islands

source.title: Key Climate Messages for September to November 2026

events.title: Rainy season starts late on Java, Bali and Nusa Tenggara
events.likelihood: late onset predicted in 529 seasonal zones (61.08% of land area)
events.place: Java, Bali, West and East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia
events.why: BMKG predicts a late rainy season in 529 seasonal zones covering 61.08% of Indonesia's land and attributes it to a very strong El Nino together with the Indian Ocean Dipole. Most of Java, Bali, NTB and NTT only start in December. BMKG warns of drought and land and forest fires, especially in September and October.
events.quote: Kemudian musim hujan bulan Desember dialami sebagian Lampung, sebagian besar Jawa, sebagian Kalimantan Selatan (Kalsel), sebagian besar Bali, sebagian besar NTB, sebagian besar NTT

source.title: BMKG: El Niño Sangat Kuat sedang Terjadi, Musim Hujan 2026/2027 Diprediksi Datang Lebih Lambat
source.publisher: BMKG (Indonesian Agency for Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics)

events.title: Greater Horn short rains: wetter than normal
events.likelihood: probability > 90% of wetter-than-average (strongest signal in the region)
events.place: Southern Ethiopia, central and southern Somalia, north-eastern Kenya
events.why: ICPAC's consensus outlook for the October to December rains, which bring up to 70% of annual rain in parts of the region. The forum links it to a strong El Nino and a developing positive Indian Ocean Dipole, with 1997 and 2023 as analogue years.
events.quote: The strongest signal for wetter-than-average conditions (probability > 90%) is forecast over southern Ethiopia, central to southern Somalia, and north-eastern Kenya.

source.title: Technical Statement from the 74th Greater Horn of Africa Climate Outlook Forum (GHACOF74)
source.publisher: ICPAC (IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre)

events.title: Somalia river valleys: severe flooding expected
events.likelihood: expected in FEWS NET's most likely scenario; credible risk of Famine (IPC Phase 5) from October to January
events.place: Juba and Shabelle river valleys, southern Somalia (point at Jowhar)
events.why: FEWS NET's most likely scenario has riverine flooding during the deyr rains, with Emergency (IPC Phase 4) outcomes in parts of the south. It cites the strong El Nino and a likely strong positive IOD, with 2023 as the likely analogue and 1997, the worst flood year on record, as the worst case. Flooding would disrupt cropping and farm labour.
events.quote: Severe flooding is expected to inundate riverine areas, cut them off from markets and services, and cause asset losses.

source.title: Somalia Food Security Outlook Update August 2026 - January 2027: Risk of Famine (IPC Phase 5) persists despite better-than-anticipated xagaa rains

events.title: Wetter fall and winter favoured on the US southern Plains
events.likelihood: 40-50% chance above normal at most, fall and winter seasons
events.place: US southern Plains (Texas, Oklahoma)
events.why: CPC's El Nino composites show a robust wet signal from the Four Corners across the southern Plains to the Southeast coast from October to December, and the wet signal stays dominant through winter. Odds peak at 70-80 percent over southern Georgia and northern Florida.
events.quote: Over the southern Plains, probabilities for above normal precipitation reach a maximum of 40-50 percent

source.title: Prognostic Discussion for Long-Lead Seasonal Outlooks

events.title: South Africa maize belt: below-normal rain
events.likelihood: below-normal rainfall is the most likely outcome
events.place: Most of South Africa (point in the Free State summer grain area)
events.why: South African Weather Service seasonal forecast, reported by the government news agency. SAWS says the November to January forecast is very similar to October to December. It also notes the very strong 1997/98 El Nino brought slightly above-normal rain to parts of the summer rainfall region, so drought is likely but not certain.
events.quote: SAWS’ latest seasonal forecast for October to December 2026 indicates that below-normal rainfall is the most likely outcome over most of South Africa.

source.title: SAWS warns of very strong El Nino and hotter, drier spring conditions
source.publisher: SAnews (South African Government News Agency), reporting the South African Weather Service

events.title: Zimbabwe: below-normal rain through the season
events.likelihood: high probability of below-normal rainfall for Oct to Dec; below normal in most areas for Jan to Mar (normal to below normal in the south and west)
events.place: Zimbabwe (nationwide)
events.why: Zimbabwe's national outlook links the forecast to El Nino and a positive IOD and names 2015/16 and 2023/24 as analogues, both with a widespread failed onset. It says a significant part of the country may see no effective start to the season, and that both halves of the season show a dry signal.
events.quote: the forecast indicates a high probability of below-normal rainfall nationwide for the October–December 2026 period

source.title: Zimbabwe National Climate Outlook: No.1 October 2026 to March 2027

events.title: Southern Madagascar: below-normal rain
events.likelihood: increased chances of below-normal rainfall
events.place: Southern Madagascar (point in Androy)
events.why: SARCOF-33 zone 8 for November to January. For October to December it gives normal to below normal for western and southwestern Madagascar, and for December to February the south shifts to normal to above normal, so the dry signal is strongest in November to January.
events.quote: Zone 8: Southern Madagascar. Increased chances of below-normal rainfall.

source.title: Statement from the Thirty-Third Southern Africa Regional Climate Outlook Forum (SARCOF-33)

events.title: Heavy rain episodes on Peru's north coast from November
events.likelihood: above normal rain expected; moderate to strong rain episodes possible from November
events.place: North coast of Peru (point in Piura)
events.why: ENFEN keeps its Coastal El Nino Alert and rates an extraordinary Coastal El Nino as most likely from September 2026 to January 2027. It expects river flows above normal in the north mainly from November, and rain above historical averages on the north and central coast and the western northern highlands in summer 2027.
events.quote: se esperan condiciones por encima de lo normal en la costa norte, con posibles episodios de lluvias de moderada a fuerte intensidad desde noviembre

source.title: Comunicado Oficial ENFEN N° 16-2026
source.publisher: ENFEN, Comision Multisectorial encargada del Estudio Nacional del Fenomeno El Nino (Peru)

events.title: Drought spreading across the Visayas by February
events.likelihood: dry condition by end of November, dry spell by end of December and January, drought by end of February 2027 (PAGASA categories)
events.place: Visayas, Philippines (Cebu, Bohol, Negros, Leyte, Samar, Siquijor, Biliran)
events.why: PAGASA's drought outlook of 3 Sep, based on rain to 31 August and its 6-month forecast, moves these 11 provinces from dry condition at the end of November to dry spell at the ends of December and January and drought at the end of February 2027. It lists 21 provinces nationwide in drought by the end of February.
events.quote: Biliran, Bohol, Cebu, Eastern Samar, Leyte, Negros Occidental, Negros Oriental, Northern Samar, Samar (Western Samar), Siquijor, Southern Leyte

source.title: Dry Spell / Drought Assessment and Outlook
source.publisher: PAGASA (Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration)

events.title: Northern Pakistan: wetter winter start
events.likelihood: expected above-average precipitation
events.place: Northern and central Pakistan (Gilgit-Baltistan, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, northern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, central and eastern Punjab)
events.why: FEWS NET expects above-average rain and snow in December and January, the start of the winter wet season, across the north and centre. This follows a poor monsoon in Sindh, Balochistan and parts of Punjab and a likely below-average kharif harvest.
events.quote: El Niño conditions in late 2026 and early 2027 are expected to result in above-average precipitation to start the winter wet season

source.title: Pakistan Food Security Outlook Update August 2026 - January 2027: Kharif harvest will most likely be below average, driven by poor monsoon rains

events.title: Southern and central Malawi: dry late season
events.likelihood: expected below-normal; increased likelihood of prolonged dry spells around February
events.place: Southern and central Malawi
events.why: DCCMS expects a much delayed onset in the south, then below-normal January to March rain and prolonged dry spells around February. Its indicative crop water index points to a 13 to 31 percent production drop against 2025/26 in the south and centre. The north is expected normal to above normal.
events.quote: January to March (JFM) is expected to have below-normal rainfall over southern and central Malawi

source.title: The 2026-2027 Seasonal Climate Outlook
source.publisher: Department of Climate Change and Meteorological Services (DCCMS), Malawi

events.title: Below normal rain likely in Peru's southeastern highlands
events.likelihood: 46% chance below normal, the most likely category, for January to March 2027
events.place: Southeastern highlands of Peru (Ayacucho, Apurimac, Cusco, Arequipa, Puno)
events.why: SENAMHI's summer 2027 scenario calibrates NMME and ECMWF runs initialised in September 2026 and names the developing El Nino as the key factor for the season. January to March holds the largest rainfall totals of the rainy season. The scenario is updated monthly until November 2026.
events.quote: El escenario más probable indica lluvias inferiores a lo normal (46%).

source.title: Escenario probabilistico de lluvias y temperaturas verano 2027 (Informe Tecnico N°11-2026/SENAMHI-DMCA-SVC)

events.title: Central and southern SADC: dry January to March
events.likelihood: expected; below-normal rainfall
events.place: Angola, Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Zambia, parts of South Africa (point in southern Zambia)
events.why: SADC's regional consensus for the second half of the season. Southern Mozambique, northern South Africa, Eswatini, Lesotho and Madagascar are expected normal to below normal, while the DRC, northern Zambia, northern Malawi, northern Mozambique and parts of Tanzania are expected normal to above normal.
events.quote: The January to March (JFM) 2027 period is expected to have below-normal rainfall over most of the central and southern parts of the SADC region

source.title: Statement from the Thirty-Third Southern Africa Regional Climate Outlook Forum (SARCOF-33)
